translation_notes: None of the four Namespace(...) objects (p, skos, rdfs, dpv_owl) escapes the function -- only the URIRef terms they produce (risk_uri, barn_uri, analysis_uri, check_uri, all reused later as subject or object) leave the block, and a prefixed name resolves to a plain URIRef immediately, so this region is a clean case of the stratum's target construction, not one of the not-expressible ones the batch instructions warned about.

PREFIX comes from an import, not a literal in the source, so `p` cannot be `@prefix p: <...> .` with a literal IRI; used `@prefix p: f<{PREFIX}> .` instead -- the formatted-IRI form the reference documents for exactly this case. f<...> joins holes verbatim with no percent-encoding, so f<{PREFIX}> is safe here: the whole value is one hole and there is no surrounding literal text to protect.

the four `.add()` calls sharing a subject (three per block) are fused into one `+{ s p1 o1 ; p2 o2 ; p3 o3 }` per block (add_run_shared_subject's construction), the most specific form available -- keeping four separate `+{ }` per block would have been a needless downgrade.

context_shim.py supplies PREFIX and stub versions of the other acro.ontology_handler imports the region's import statement names but never calls, so the import line still executes identically on both sides.
